newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH SHORT-DATED MONEY RATES STILL UNDER PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH SHORT-DATED MONEY RATES STILL UNDER PRESSURE.

text.p: Dutch short-dated money rates remained under upward pressure on Wednesday as the allocation under the current special advances pact, which expires on Thursday, was somewhat tight, dealers said.
Dealers said the special advances rate of 2.50 percent was likely to remain unchanged when the central bank sets a new pact this afternoon at 1500 GMT.
Subscriptions to the new special advances pact will be open early on Thursday and allocations will be announced shortly afterwards at around 0900 GMT.
"It depends very much on the size of the allocation, what call money rates will do," said one dealer.
But he expected the rate would come off its recent high.
The current allocation of 3.74 billion guilders under a six-day pact has been tight from the start.
Call was bid six to seven basis points higher at around 2.81-2.87 percent versus a range of 2.75-2.81 on Tuesday.
One-month deposits added four basis points to 2.88 percent bid.
Dealers said the weakening of the guilder against the mark had no effect on the money market.
"The guilder rate versus the mark has not come to a critical stage yet," the dealer said.
The guilder was trading at 112.20 per 100 marks from 112.1850 on Tuesday.
